items.followUp: Explain the formation of an ionic bond between magnesium and oxygen atoms.

rubric.why: An ionic bond is defined by electron transfer and the resulting attraction between oppositely charged ions.
rubric.how: Award for identifying electron transfer as the basis of an ionic bond.

rubric.why: Sodium transfers its outer electron to chlorine, forming the ions needed for the bond.
rubric.how: Award when both sodium’s loss and chlorine’s gain of one electron are stated.

rubric.why: The oppositely charged sodium and chloride ions attract to form the ionic bond in sodium chloride.
rubric.how: Award when both ions and the electrostatic attraction between them are identified.

modelAnswer: An ionic bond is a chemical bond formed by the transfer of electrons, followed by the electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions.
A sodium atom has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 1, while a chlorine atom has the configuration 2, 8, 7.
Sodium loses one electron: Na → Na+ + e-.
Chlorine gains one electron: Cl + e- → Cl-.
The oppositely charged Na+ and Cl- ions attract each other electrostatically, forming an ionic bond in sodium chloride, NaCl.

items.followUp: Give two differences between crystalline and amorphous solids.

rubric.why: Crystalline solids have an orderly arrangement and definite shape, whereas amorphous solids have an irregular arrangement and no definite shape.
rubric.how: Award for comparing the arrangement and shape of both types of solid.

rubric.why: Crystalline solids have a sharp melting point.
rubric.how: Award when a sharp melting point is associated with crystalline solids.

accept: soften over a range of temperatures
rubric.why: Amorphous solids soften over a range of temperatures and do not have a sharp melting point.
rubric.how: Award when the range of softening or lack of a sharp melting point is associated with amorphous solids.

modelAnswer: Crystalline solids have particles arranged in a regular arrangement and have a definite geometrical shape; amorphous solids have an irregular arrangement and no definite geometrical shape.
Crystalline solids have a sharp melting point; amorphous solids soften over a range of temperatures and have no sharp melting point.

items.followUp: Define solubility and state how temperature affects the solubility of gases in liquids.

rubric.why: Solubility is the maximum amount of solute that forms a saturated solution under stated conditions.
rubric.how: Award for defining solubility in terms of the maximum amount of solute that forms a saturated solution.

rubric.why: The standard expression gives the amount of solute dissolved in 100 g of solvent at a stated temperature.
rubric.how: Award for including both the 100 g solvent basis and a specified temperature.

rubric.why: The solubility of most solid solutes in liquids increases as temperature increases.
rubric.how: Award when increasing temperature is linked to increasing solubility of most solids.

rubric.why: The solubility of gases in liquids generally decreases as temperature increases.
rubric.how: Award when increasing temperature is linked to decreasing gas solubility.

modelAnswer: Solubility is the maximum amount of solute, in grams, that dissolves in 100 g of solvent to form a saturated solution at a specified temperature.
As temperature increases, the solubility of most solid solutes in liquids increases.
As temperature increases, the solubility of gases in liquids generally decreases.
